title: Privileged access event ledger rotation and residency-aware retention controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a resilient, region-aware append-only event ledger for privileged admin activity (access grants, role changes, config updates) with automated retention enforcement. The ledger will support cryptographic signing via HSM, object lifecycle rotation policies tied to customer residency, and an evidence export path for compliance reporting. This work focuses on the server-side write path, retention controller, SLOs for ingest/repair, and an audit UI hook for the Console team.
acceptance_criteria: All admin events emitted to the ledger include immutable metadata: timestamp, region tag, actor, change diff, and HSM signature fingerprint

Retention controller enforces regional retention policies: events with EU residency tag retained a minimum of 7 years, US-tagged events retained per contract, with automated expiry manifests generated
Ledger supports rotation without losing append-only guarantees: rotated segments are attestable and remain queryable via read API
Export endpoint produces tamper-evident evidence bundles (signed manifest + segment checksums) consumable by legal/compliance teams
Performance: write p95 latency <120ms under 500 rps burst; background rotation/compaction does not increase write error rate
E2E tests and load tests added to CI; Console can display per-customer retention status and next-expiry dates
tasks: Design HSM signing scheme and integrate with KMS team (spec + threat model)
Schema: extend admin-event envelope with residency, retention_policy_id, and rotation_id
Server: implement append-only writer with leasing to prevent double-writes during rotation
Retention controller: policy engine that reconciles desired retention vs actual storage, emits remediation jobs
Rotation worker: snapshot + rotate segments, compute checksums, write signed manifest
Export API: bundle generator (manifest + index + signed checksum) + access controls
Console hook: add retention status and expiry timeline to audit dashboards
Add integration tests, load test scenarios, and failure-injection cases (HSM unavailability, region outage)
Run security review and threat model sign-off before canary
decisions: Use existing KMS/HSM cluster for signing rather than embedding keys in app tier to reduce blast radius
Retention policies modeled as named objects (retention-policy-id) instead of inline durations to support future policy versioning
Prefer region-tagging at emit time (service layer) rather than deriving region during ingestion to keep provenance clear
Export bundles will be immutable objects stored in a cold tier (S3/Blob) with lifecycle governed by legal hold flag
comments: 2026-02-14 - Marco: Initial spike complete. HSM latency looks acceptable (median 25ms) but we need batching of signature requests to avoid rate limits.
2026-02-20 - PM (Lina Zhou): Confirmed legal requires separate custody for EU-restricted evidence exports. Marking as high customer impact for EU customers.
2026-02-25 - Security (Jared): Threat model reviewed. We must add replay-protection headers and a per-segment monotonic counter to prevent signature reuse.
2026-03-02 - Design review: Console team requested a lightweight retention timeline widget; added API fields for next_expiry_date and retention_policy_description.
2026-03-07 - Load test: 30m soak at 1k rps; observed rotation worker spike in IO—adding rate limiter and backoff to rotation to smooth throughput.
implementation_notes: Writer will append to region-local persistent queue (replicated) and ack after durable write + HSM signature fingerprint persisted. Rotation will perform background checksum, generate signed manifest via HSM, and mark segment sealed. Sealed segments remain readable; delete is performed by retention controller after cross-region replication checks and export generation for legal hold. Use existing object-store adapter and add a segment index for fast range reads.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary to non-production tenant group for 48h; 2) Canary to internal-prod (security and compliance teams) 72h; 3) Gradual tenant opt-in starting with low-traffic customers and EU-region customers; 4) Full-on enforcement after 3 weeks if no regressions. Fallback: disable retention enforcement and continue writes to legacy audit topic.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope schema and signature validation, integration tests for rotation+export, chaos tests simulating HSM latency and network partitions, load tests for write path and rotation under 1k rps, QA verification of Console views and export bundles.
